target: def Target : Prop := ∀ T : Set Form, Def14 T (neg (ex 1 Def16))

translation: Target is the proposition asserting that for every set of formulas T : Set Form (with no restrictions on T, including T = ∅), the formula ¬∃x₁ ∀x₀ (K(¬R₀(x₀, x₀)) ↔ R₀(x₁, x₀)) is derivable from T in the proof system Def14. Explicitly, in the formal language Form—built from binary atomic formulas atom r x y (for natural numbers r, x, y), falsity (fls), implication (imp), universal quantification (all), and a unary modal operator (K), with defined abbreviations ¬φ := imp φ fls, φ ∧ ψ := ¬(φ → ¬ψ), φ ↔ ψ := (φ → ψ) ∧ (ψ → φ), and ∃x φ := ¬∀x ¬φ—writing R₀(a, b) for atom 0 a b (Def15 a b), x₀ for variable 0, and x₁ for variable 1, the formula asserted to be derivable is neg (ex 1 Def16), where Def16 is all 0 (iff (K (neg (atom 0 0 0))) (atom 0 1 0)). Note that K appears only on ¬R₀(x₀, x₀) on the left-hand side of the biconditional, and not outside the quantifiers. Derivability from T (Def14 T) is defined inductively by three rules: (1) any formula in Def13 is derivable, where Def13 consists of all formulas in Def12 together with all formulas of the form K ψ for ψ in Def12, and Def12 is the closure under universal generalization (all x) of the base axioms Def11—namely, all propositional tautologies (formulas true under every valuation v : Form → Prop with ¬v(fls) and v(φ → ψ) ↔ (v(φ) → v(ψ))), universal instantiation (∀x φ) → φ[y/x] whenever y is free for x in φ (no free occurrence of x lies in the scope of a quantifier binding y), quantifier distribution (∀x (φ → ψ)) → (∀x φ → ∀x ψ), vacuous quantification φ → ∀x φ whenever x is not free in φ, modal distribution K(φ → ψ) → (K φ → K ψ), K φ → φ, K φ → K(K φ), and K(∀x φ) → ∀x (K φ); (2) every hypothesis φ ∈ T is derivable; and (3) modus ponens: if φ → ψ and φ are derivable from T, then ψ is derivable from T. No rules of universal generalization or necessitation apply to arbitrary derivations in Def14 T (universal generalization is confined to Def12, and a single application of K is confined to Def13).

divergences.description: The outer modal operator K (Reinhardt's B) is missing from the formalized sentence. Reinhardt's Theorem 5 asserts the inconsistency of ∃e B∀x(Bp(x) ↔ U(e,x)) (proved via ∃e ∀x B(Bp(x) ↔ U(e,x))), and the author's claim likewise specifies ∃e B∀x(B¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)). However, Def16 is ∀x₀ (K(¬U(x₀,x₀)) ↔ U(x₁,x₀)) and Target asserts derivability of neg (ex 1 Def16), i.e. ¬∃x₁ ∀x₀ (K(¬U(x₀,x₀)) ↔ U(x₁,x₀)), with no K outside ∀x₀ or the biconditional. Without that outer K, the sentence is consistent in Def14 (it holds at the root of a two-world reflexive-transitive constant-domain Kripke model with singleton domain {0} where U(0,0) is false at the root and true at the accessible world), making Target false for T = ∅.

Reinhardt's Theorem 5 states the inconsistency of a schema over arbitrary formulas p(x) and a two-variable formula U(e,x), whereas Target specializes to the single diagonal instance p(x) := ¬U(x,x) used in the proof (a harmless strengthening for proving the schema inconsistent) and fixes U to a single primitive binary relation symbol (atom 0) rather than an arbitrary two-variable formula. Both limitations are noted in the author's claim.

Compared to the full system in [P-R323], the context uses a pure first-order modal fragment without arithmetic, equality, constants, or function symbols (a declared limitation, and a harmless strengthening for proving inconsistency), and Def13 permits K ψ for open formulas ψ ∈ Def12 rather than only closed sentences (equivalent in the presence of kall and inst).

judgement.summary: Target is divergent from Reinhardt's Theorem 5 because it omits the outer modal operator B (K) in ∃e B∀x(B¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)), instead asserting the refutability of ∃e ∀x(B¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)). That omission fundamentally alters the claim and renders Target unprovable (false) in the defined logic, since the formula without the outer K is consistent.
